entries.title: Psalms 135:1
segments:
. A Psalm of praise, in which God's relations to His Church, His power in the natural world, and in delivering His people, are contrasted with the vanity of idols and idol-worship. 
 
    1-3. In the general call for praise, the priests, that stand in the house of the Lord, are specially mentioned.

entries.title: Psalms 135:4
segments: 4-7. God's choice of Israel is the first reason assigned for rendering praise; the next, His manifested greatness in creation and providence.

entries.title: Psalms 135:6
segments: 6. heaven, and ... seas, and all ... ends of the earth--denote universality.

entries.title: Psalms 135:8
segments: ] is cited to illustrate His "tokens and wonders."

entries.title: Psalms 135:10
segments: 10-12. The conquest of Canaan was by God's power, not that of the people.

entries.title: Psalms 135:13
segments:
13. heritage--or, "possession." 
 
    name ... memorial--Each denote that by which God is made known.

entries.title: Psalms 135:18
segments: 18. are like unto them--or, "shall be like," &c. Idolaters become spiritually stupid and perish with their idols (

entries.title: Psalms 135:21
segments: ). From the Church, as a center, His praise is diffused throughout the earth.
